doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: The three Dizzy Gillespies
summary: Dizzy the screwball, John Gillespie the spiritual man, and the deeply serious musician.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And it was deep, deep, deep stuff. There were three Dizzy Gillespies. There was Dizzy the screwball that everybody knows. Then there was John Gillespie, who was the very spiritual man. I called him John. I didn’t call him Dizzy in the later years. And then there was the very serious musician. He would be a nut until he put his horn up and then this look would come over him and he was serious as a heart attack. I’d be looking at him and say, “Uh oh.” And he’d be in this place and the music would be coming off the piano at me man. I said, “Where’d that come from? Where’d that come from?” And I’d just go.

No. And he too, he had a depth to it, a depth I would say is comparable to classical music, some of those composers, like Beethoven. He had a depth. Dizzy had a perfection in his music that I would say is close as a human being can get, the depth of his music.
